Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The main planning problem is that the station has a reliable morning audience, but its evening programs have shifted around several times since the library began renovating its meeting room. The station manager mentioned one possible change during the last handover and said “we can move the harbor report after the school bulletin”. Please retain that as a reported suggestion rather than a confirmed change. The school bulletin is a three minute recorded item delivered by the district office and currently plays at seven forty five on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The phrase harbor report means the short ferry and tide update within Morning Harbor, not the whole program. If the schedule request asks about moving it, the producers should be asked to note whether the change would leave enough time for the eight fifteen notice board and should not assume that the district office will alter its delivery time.

1. Suggest two possible Friday times for the archive conversation and identify who will check whether a studio guest slot is available.

Do not add a decision about the Greenhouse Hour because its regular pattern is already known, and do not present the Saturday Kitchen Table equipment request as an unresolved program time. The numbered items should be easy to read, but the rest of the prompt can use ordinary paragraphs.

There are practical details to include in the schedule request. The station has one portable recorder that is shared with the youth media club on Tuesday evenings, and the larger microphone is kept in a labeled cabinet beside the sound desk. A presenter who needs either item should be named in the schedule so the volunteers can arrange a handoff. The station has no regular producer on Sunday, and the building caretaker locks the side entrance at five thirty. The schedule should also distinguish a studio session from a broadcast slot because people have occasionally mistaken one for the other.

Please ask the producers to flag any conflict they cannot settle at that handover and leave the next step open rather than prescribing who must approve it.
